name: aqg-session-handoff
description: Generate a paste-ready cross-session handoff prompt that lets a next-session LLM cold-start on a generic project — repo/branch + environment, what is done and verified, current working state, next steps, discipline traps, the first concrete action, and open decisions. Two modes — `new` prints an 8-section skeleton (Done-so-far prefilled from the construction ledger when present); `validate` reads the filled handoff from stdin and gates it (8 sections present, no placeholder or secret residue, plus first-step / actor / audit-state checks) before paste. For a generic project session handoff WITHOUT EAF engine run state — if the repo is running an EAF engine, use eaf-session-handoff instead (it captures run_id / hold-gate / transition_log, which this does not); for a completion product HANDOFF.md, use eaf-handoff. Use at session boundaries, high context, after compaction, or when the user asks for a handoff to continue next session. Not a substitute for aqg-evidence-closeout (in-session completion evidence).

sentence_patterns: 我 CTX 快满了, 给我生成一个 handoff 让下个 session 接着干
帮我写个 paste-ready 交接 prompt, 下一棒冷启动用
session 要结束了, 把当前状态/下一步/踩过的坑整理成交接
compaction 之后, 整理一份 cross-session handoff 给下个 session
Run aqg-session-handoff new to emit an 8-section handoff skeleton

cli_contract.0: success — new printed 8-section skeleton to stdout OR validate gate passed
cli_contract.1: validation failure — validate found a gate violation (R1-R8); details on stderr
cli_contract.2: usage error — bad args or missing subcommand (argparse)

owner_only_actions: read-only: prints skeleton to stdout (new) / gates stdin (validate); never writes the filesystem, never pushes/merges/deploys; the user owns running validate before paste and the paste itself

cases.prompt: My CTX is nearly full — generate a handoff so the next session can pick up where I left off
Write me a paste-ready handoff prompt for the next session to cold-start with
The session is wrapping up — organize the current state / next steps / traps hit into a handoff
After compaction, put together a cross-session handoff for the next session
Use /aqg-session-handoff new to produce an 8-section handoff skeleton
